PropNex Malaysia
The Insider Edge

上週一 Rising Millionaire，Ally Wong 講的 GTA 深耕。滿房子人聽同一場分享，同樣的內容在每個人手上會出現嗎？不會。

但每次這樣的活動結束後，我們都會看到一個很可惜的狀況：很多人去了，拍了照，然後那些照片就留在手機相簿裡。

這一期，我們想在你走進會場之前，先說清楚三件事。

1. 鏡頭對準什麼

鏡頭對準什麼，決定你能說什麼故事

Story 的素材不是越多越好，而是要對準幾個有內容力的時刻。

第一類是知識型素材：臺上 Leader 或嘉賓說了一句讓你有感的話，截圖或錄一小段，加上你的一句話發出去，馬上就有內容價值。

第二類是規模型素材：兩百個 Leader 在同一個房間、一臺要被抽走的車擺在會場中央、從新加坡飛過來的老闆站在臺上，這些畫面傳遞的是「我在一間認真做事的公司」，不用多說什麼，鏡頭帶到就夠了。

第三類是關係型素材：你跟同事或 Leader 的合照、活動中的一個互動時刻。這類內容讓你的 Story 有溫度，也讓觀眾看到你是誰的圈子裡的人。

進場之前先想好你要抓的三個時刻，素材就不會只是停在相簿裡。

2. 文字決定你是打卡還是品牌

同樣一張照，文字角度決定你是打卡還是做品牌

拍到素材是第一步，文字才是讓 Story 真正發揮作用的地方。

行銷上有一個概念叫做 Value Framing，說的是同樣一件事，從不同角度說出來，在別人心裡建立的形象完全不一樣。同樣是參加一個公司活動，你可以說「出席 Rising Millionaire」，也可以說「今天在場聽到 Ally 一句話，讓我重新想了一件事」。前者是打卡，後者是在說你怎麼看這個行業。

就算你這次沒有到場，這個邏輯一樣適用。公司公布了一件事、活動傳出了什麼動態，你用自己的角度回應，說說「這讓我想到」或「我選擇在這裡的原因之一，就是這個」，一樣是在做個人品牌。你說的是公司，傳遞的是你。

同一張照，兩個方向：一個讓人知道你在場，一個讓人想認識你這個人。

3. Story 的頻率就是存在感

Story 的頻率，就是你在 IG 裡的存在感

很多人會覺得發太多 Story 是在打擾人，但 Instagram 的邏輯剛好相反。

Story 的排序是按照時間走的，你最近發的 Story 就排在關注者 Story 欄的最前面。活動當天你每發一篇 Story，就等於重新出現在他們眼前一次。整天下來，我們建議至少 5 篇，讓你的名字在這一天裡一直出現在最顯眼的位置。

Story 同時也是你跟關注者之間關係最直接的一條線。當有人對你的 Story 傳了 DM 給你，Instagram 把這個記為一個強訊號，知道你們之間有真實互動，之後也會把你的內容推給他更多。這就像你在一個場合裡跟某個人聊起來了，之後他就開始記得你，Instagram 也是同樣的邏輯。

一整天至少 5 篇，不用每篇都精彩，讓人看到「你今天在」，就已經是在建立存在感了。

Story 不是為了說一件大事，是為了讓人習慣看到你。

下禮拜就有一場大活動了。全馬各地的 Leader 聚集在同一個地方，我們的新加坡老闆和四位老闆也都會出席。這樣的時刻不常有，不管你有沒有在現場，每一場活動都會是你最好的素材。

下一期，我們繼續說：活動結束之後，怎麼把同樣的素材，開始吸引人加入你的團隊。

Next week, 200 leaders are all showing up in one room. Our Singapore boss is flying over just for this. It's that kind of event.

And every time something like this happens, we see the same pattern: people attend, snap a few photos, and those photos never leave their gallery.

Before you walk through those doors, here are three things worth knowing.

1. Know What to Shoot

Know what to shoot before you shoot anything

It's not about shooting everything. It's about knowing which moments are worth capturing.

The first type: insight moments. A speaker says something that hits. Screenshot it, record a quick clip, add one line of your own — that's a Story with something to say.

The second type: scale moments. Two hundred leaders in one room. A car on stage about to be given away. The boss from Singapore at the front. You don't need to explain these — they speak for themselves. "I'm at a company that means business."

The third type: connection moments. A photo with a colleague, a candid moment with a leader, the in-between scenes. These are what make your content feel real instead of curated.

Decide on three moments you want to capture before you walk in. That's what stops the photos from living in your gallery forever.

2. Caption Makes the Brand

Same photo. Different caption. Completely different brand.

Capturing content is step one. But your words are what make a Story actually land.

There's a concept in marketing called Value Framing. The idea is simple: the same moment, told from a different angle, builds a completely different impression. You can post "Proud to be at Rising Millionaire" — or you can post "Something Ally said on stage on stage today that I keep thinking about." One is a check-in. The other is a point of view.

This works even if you're not going. When the company shares something, when a moment gets picked up — respond with your own angle. "This is exactly why I chose to be here." You're talking about the company. But people are seeing you.

Same photo, two directions: one tells people you were there, the other makes them want to know who you are.

3. Post Often, Stay Visible

The more you post, the more you show up

A lot of people hold back because they think posting too many Stories feels like spamming. Instagram actually thinks the opposite.

Stories are ranked by recency — the most recent one sits at the front of your followers' Story tray. Every time you post during the event, you move back to the front. Aim for at least 5 Stories throughout the day, and your name stays visible all day, not just once.

Stories are also the most direct line between you and the people who follow you. When someone DMs you because of a Story, Instagram treats that as a strong signal. It sees a real connection, and it keeps showing your content to that person. Think of it like actually having a conversation at an event instead of just being in the room. People remember the ones who talked to them.

Five Stories minimum. They don't all need to be perfect. Let people see that you were there — that presence alone is how you stay top of mind.

Stories aren't about saying one big thing. They're about making it a habit for people to see you.

Next week is big. Leaders from across Malaysia, our Singapore boss, and all four of our bosses will be in the same room. Moments like this don't come around often — whether you're there or not, every event is your best material.

Next issue, we'll show you how to use everything that comes out of this event to start attracting people to your team.
